message.content:
**Starting the Docker Engine (service) on Windows** `docker start` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker daemon itself. To bring the Docker Engine up on Windows you need to start the Docker service (or launch Docker Desktop). Here are the most common ways: | Method | What it does | How to run | |--------|--------------|------------| | **PowerShell (recommended)** | Starts the Docker service (`com.docker.service`) | ```powershell
Start-Service -Name Docker
``` | | **Command Prompt** | Same as above but using `net` | ```cmd
net start com.docker.service
``` | | **Docker Desktop GUI** | Launches the Docker Desktop app, which automatically starts the service | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon from the Start menu or taskbar. | > **Tip:** If you’re running Docker Desktop, the service name is `com.docker.service`. If you installed Docker Engine via the Windows Server Docker Engine, the service name may simply be `Docker`. --- ### Starting a specific container If you actually meant to start a container named `my_container`, you would run: ```bash docker start my_container ``` Replace `my_container` with the name or ID of the container you wish to start. --- #### Quick one‑liner (PowerShell) ```powershell Start-Service Docker ``` This will start the Docker service if it’s not already running. After that, you can verify with: ```powershell Get-Service Docker ``` You should see `Status : Running`. Let me know if you need help starting a particular container or if you’re encountering any errors!
